question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

48, 146, 440, ? , 3968, 11906, 35720
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 1322.

GIVEN

• 48, 146, 440, ? , 3968, 11906, 35720

SOLUTION

• The pattern is (previous term × 3) + 2.

• 48 × 3 + 2 = 146

• 146 × 3 + 2 = 440

• 440 × 3 + 2 = 1322

• Check: 1322 × 3 + 2 = 3968 ✓

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Each next number is roughly 3 times the previous; 440 × 3 = 1320, add 2 → 1322.

NOTE

• For multiplicative series, divide consecutive terms (146/48 ≈ 3) to spot the ×3 rule, then find the small constant added (+2).

question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

?, E, I, N, T, A, I, R
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. B.

GIVEN

• ?, E, I, N, T, A, I, R

SOLUTION

• Position values: E=5, I=9, N=14, T=20, A=27(1), I=35(9), R=44(18).

• Gaps increase: +4, +5, +6, +7, +8, +9.

• So before E the gap should be +3, meaning ? = 5 − 3 = 2 = B.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Differences form 3,4,5,6,7,8,9; back-count from E (5) by 3 to get B (2).

NOTE

• Convert letters to A=1…Z=26 (allowing wrap after Z) to expose arithmetic gap patterns quickly.

question:
Select the option that is related to the fifth letter cluster in the same way as the second letter cluster is related to the first letter cluster and fourth letter cluster is related to third letter cluster.

HX : JB :: BV : DZ :: NU : ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. PY.

GIVEN

• HX : JB :: BV : DZ :: NU : ?

SOLUTION

• Rule: 1st letter +2, 2nd letter +4.

• HX → J(H+2), B(X+4=28→B). BV → D(B+2), Z(V+4).

• NU → P(N+2), Y(U+4=25→Y) = PY.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Just shift first letter by +2 and second by +4 on the given pair.

NOTE

• When X/V etc. cross Z, subtract 26 to wrap (X+4 = 28−26 = 2 = B).

question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

MJ, KD, IX, GR, EL, CF, ?, YT
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. AZ.

GIVEN

• MJ, KD, IX, GR, EL, CF, ?, YT

SOLUTION

• First letters: M,K,I,G,E,C,… decrease by 2 → next = A (C−2).

• Second letters: J,D,X,R,L,F,… decrease by 6 → F−6 = Z (6−6=0→26).

• So missing term = AZ.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Track the two letter-columns separately: −2 and −6 with wrap-around.

NOTE

• Two-letter series usually hide two independent step patterns; split the columns.

question:
In the following question, set of letter clusters are given. The letter clusters of each set are related to the letter clusters of the same set by some Logic/Rule/Relation. From the given alternatives, select a group of letter clusters which follows the same Logic/Rule/Relation.

(GM, EJ, CG)

(MS, KP, IM)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. (FN, DK, BH).

GIVEN

• Sample sets: (GM, EJ, CG) and (MS, KP, IM).

SOLUTION

• In each set the first letters fall by 2 (G,E,C) and second letters fall by 3 (M,J,G).

• Gaps within a cluster: G→M=6, E→J=5, C→G=4 (decrease by 1).

• Option (FN, DK, BH): first letters F,D,B (−2), second N,K,H (−3), gaps 8,7,6 (−1). Same rule.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Look for first-letter −2, second-letter −3 across the three clusters.

NOTE

• For 'set matching', find one consistent rule (letter steps and internal gap) that all members obey.

question: What will be the product of the number of Mondays and Saturdays in the month of August in the year 2012?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 16.

GIVEN

• Month = August 2012 (31 days).

SOLUTION

• 1 August 2012 was a Wednesday.

• 31 days = 4 weeks + 3 extra days → the extra days fall on Wed, Thu, Fri (these occur 5 times).

• Hence Mondays occur 4 times and Saturdays occur 4 times.

• Product = 4 × 4 = 16.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• In a 31-day month only the 1st day's weekday and the next two weekdays occur 5 times; all others occur 4 times.

NOTE

• 1 Jan 2012 = Sunday; days up to 1 Aug = 213, 213 mod 7 = 3 → Wednesday.

question: A person was born on 14 February 2003. What day of the week will be on his 19th birthday?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. Monday.

GIVEN

• Date of birth = 14 February 2003; 19th birthday = 14 February 2022.

SOLUTION

• 14 Feb 2003 was a Friday.

• Odd days over 19 years = 19 + 5 leap-day extras (2004,08,12,16,20) = 24; 24 mod 7 = 3.

• Friday + 3 = Monday.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Add (number of years + number of leap Feb-29s crossed) and take mod 7 to shift the weekday.

NOTE

• A normal year = 1 odd day, a leap year = 2 odd days; count only Feb-29s lying in the interval.

question: 5 persons P, Q, R, S and T are sitting in a row facing north (not necessarily in the same order). P and R are sitting at the extreme ends of the row. S is sitting to the immediate right of R. Q is sitting second to the left of P. Who is sitting to the immediate right of Q?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. T.

GIVEN

• P and R at extreme ends; S immediate right of R; Q second to left of P.

SOLUTION

• Facing north → right = higher position. S right of R means R is not the right-end, so R=1, S=2, P=5.

• Q second to left of P(5) = position 3; remaining T = position 4.

• Arrangement (left→right): R, S, Q, T, P. Immediate right of Q is T.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Fix the ends first (P,R), place S beside R, then count Q from P.

NOTE

• Facing north: person's left = our left; 'immediate right' = next seat towards the right end.

question: 7 girls A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting in a row facing north (not necessarily in the same order). D sits fifth to the right of A. D does not sit at any of the extreme ends of the row. F sits exactly in the middle of row. Two girls sit between F and B. G is third to the left of E. Who is sitting at sixth position from the left end of the row?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. D.

GIVEN

• 7 seats; D fifth to right of A, D not at ends, F in middle, two girls between F and B, G third to left of E.

SOLUTION

• A+5 = D and D not at end → A=1, D=6. F(middle)=4.

• Two girls between F(4) and B → B=7 (seat 1 is A).

• Remaining seats 2,3,5 for C,E,G with G = E−3 → E=5, G=2, C=3.

• Order: A, G, C, F, E, D, B. Sixth from left = D.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Anchor 'fifth to the right' and 'middle' first; they pin A, D and F immediately.

NOTE

• 'X third to the left of Y' means seat(X) = seat(Y) − 3.

question:
Select the option that is related to the fourth letter-number cluster in the same way as the first letter-number cluster is related to the second letter-number cluster and fifth letter-number cluster is related to sixth letter-number cluster. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

RF18 : QD36 :: ? : MH48 :: KF72 : JD144
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. NJ24.

GIVEN

• RF18 : QD36 :: ? : MH48 :: KF72 : JD144

SOLUTION

• Rule (first→second): 1st letter −1, 2nd letter −2, number ×2. Check: R−1=Q, F−2=D, 18×2=36; K−1=J, F−2=D, 72×2=144.

• So ? → MH48 must follow it: reverse gives M+1=N, H+2=J, 48÷2=24 = NJ24.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• From the pair MH48, undo the rule: +1 letter, +2 letter, halve the number.

NOTE

• Here the unknown is the 'first' of its pair, so apply the inverse operations.

question:
Select the option that is related to the first letter-number cluster in the same way as the fourth letter-number cluster is related to the third letter-number cluster and sixth letter-number cluster is related to fifth letter-number cluster. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

IM70 : ? :: BJ80 : FD200 :: JK90 : NE225
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. MG175.

GIVEN

• IM70 : ? :: BJ80 : FD200 :: JK90 : NE225

SOLUTION

• Rule (first→second): 1st letter +4, 2nd letter −6, number ×2.5. Check: B+4=F, J−6=D, 80×2.5=200; J+4=N, K−6=E, 90×2.5=225.

• Apply to IM70: I+4=M, M−6=G, 70×2.5=175 = MG175.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• 200/80 = 2.5 gives the number rule; then shift letters +4 and −6.

NOTE

• Establish the numeric multiplier from a fully-known pair before touching the letters.

question:
Select the option that is related to the fourth number in the same way as the first number is related to the second number and fifth number is related to sixth number. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

261 : 205 :: ? : 7467 :: 9011 : 8955
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 7523.

GIVEN

• 261 : 205 :: ? : 7467 :: 9011 : 8955

SOLUTION

• Rule: first − 56 = second. Check: 261 − 56 = 205; 9011 − 56 = 8955.

• So ? − 56 = 7467 → ? = 7467 + 56 = 7523.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Find the constant gap (261−205 = 56), then add it back to 7467.

NOTE

• The unknown is the larger 'first' term, so add the difference rather than subtract.

question:
Select the option that is related to the sixth number in the same way as the first number is related to the second number and third number is related to fourth number. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

187 : 567 :: 198 : 600 :: ? : 2580
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 858.

GIVEN

• 187 : 567 :: 198 : 600 :: ? : 2580

SOLUTION

• Rule: (first × 3) + 6 = second. Check: 187×3+6 = 567; 198×3+6 = 600.

• So ? × 3 + 6 = 2580 → ? × 3 = 2574 → ? = 858.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Reverse the rule on 2580: subtract 6, then divide by 3.

NOTE

• Test simple 'aX+b' forms first (×3 then +6 fits both known pairs).

question: In a certain code language, 'PANT' is coded as '102' and 'TAPE' is coded as '84'. How will 'EAST' be coded in that code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 90.

GIVEN

• PANT = 102, TAPE = 84.

SOLUTION

• Code = 2 × (sum of letter positions).

• PANT = 16+1+14+20 = 51; 51×2 = 102 ✓. TAPE = 20+1+16+5 = 42; 42×2 = 84 ✓.

• EAST = 5+1+19+20 = 45; 45×2 = 90.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Sum the alphabet positions and double it.

NOTE

• Position sum stays same for anagrams; PANT and TAPE differ only because N≠E, so their totals differ.

question: In a certain code language, 'wallet used to keep money' is coded as 'pn ta pq rs ln', 'money buys goods' is coded as 'ta pd dm', and 'goods has high price' is coded as 'dm pm tm zm'. How will 'money goods' be coded in that code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. ta dm.

GIVEN

• 'wallet used to keep money' = 'pn ta pq rs ln'

• 'money buys goods' = 'ta pd dm'

• 'goods has high price' = 'dm pm tm zm'

SOLUTION

• 'money' is common to sentence 1 and 2 → common code 'ta'.

• 'goods' is common to sentence 2 and 3 → common code 'dm'.

• So 'money goods' = ta dm.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Match a common word across two sentences to its common code.

NOTE

• Sentence 2 ('ta pd dm') shares 'ta' with S1 (money) and 'dm' with S3 (goods), fixing both words.

question:
A series is given with one term wrong. Select that wrong term from the given alternatives.

PQ707, MM587, LI469, JE350, HA231, FW112
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. MM587.

GIVEN

• PQ707, MM587, LI469, JE350, HA231, FW112

SOLUTION

• First letters should fall by 2: P,N,L,J,H,F — but term 2 shows M instead of N.

• Numbers should fall by 119: 707, 588, 469, 350, 231, 112 — but term 2 shows 587 instead of 588.

• Second letters Q,M,I,E,A,W (−4) are fine. So the wrong term is MM587 (should be NN588).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Check the number gaps (−119) — the odd one 587 breaks it, flagging that term.

NOTE

• Verify each column (1st letter, 2nd letter, number) separately to locate the misfit.

question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

YEW10, ?, WAQ22.5, VYN33.75, UWK50.625
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. XCT15.

GIVEN

• YEW10, ?, WAQ22.5, VYN33.75, UWK50.625

SOLUTION

• 1st letters: Y,X,W,V,U (−1) → missing = X.

• 2nd letters: E,C,A,Y,W (−2) → missing = C.

• 3rd letters: W,T,Q,N,K (−3) → missing = T.

• Numbers: ×1.5 each (10, 15, 22.5, 33.75, 50.625) → missing = 15.

• Term = XCT15.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Letters step −1, −2, −3 across columns; number multiplies by 1.5 (10 → 15).

NOTE

• Mixed alpha-numeric series: handle each letter column and the number independently.

question: At what time (approximately) (in PM) for the first time after 2:00 PM minute hand and hour hand of the clock will make an angle of 30 degrees?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 2:05.

GIVEN

• Time just after 2:00 PM; required angle between hands = 30°.

SOLUTION

• At 2:00 the angle is 60°. Angle at 2:00 + m min = |60 − 5.5m|.

• First time angle = 30°: 60 − 5.5m = 30 → 5.5m = 30 → m ≈ 5.45 min.

• So approximately 2:05.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Relative speed of hands = 5.5°/min; to close 30° of the 60° gap needs 30/5.5 ≈ 5.5 min.

NOTE

• Minute hand moves 6°/min, hour hand 0.5°/min → relative 5.5°/min.

question: Sum of the ages of 3 children born at interval of 5 years is 30 years. What is the age of the youngest child?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 5 years.

GIVEN

• Three children born 5 years apart; sum of ages = 30.

SOLUTION

• Let youngest = x. Ages: x, x+5, x+10.

• x + (x+5) + (x+10) = 30 → 3x + 15 = 30 → 3x = 15 → x = 5.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Middle child's age = 30 ÷ 3 = 10; youngest = 10 − 5 = 5.

NOTE

• For equally spaced values, the middle one equals the average (sum ÷ count).

question: Father's age 3 years ago from present was 5 times of the age of his son 6 years ago from present. Son's age after 7 years from present is 20 years. What is the ratio of present ages of father and son?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 38 : 13.

GIVEN

• Father 3 yrs ago = 5 × (son 6 yrs ago); son's age after 7 yrs = 20.

SOLUTION

• Son now = 20 − 7 = 13; son 6 years ago = 13 − 6 = 7.

• Father 3 years ago = 5 × 7 = 35 → father now = 35 + 3 = 38.

• Ratio = 38 : 13.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Work from the son's future age backwards, then scale father's past age and add 3.

NOTE

• Convert every 'ago/after' statement to present age first, then form the ratio.
